lineage: Provenance: this package FORKS the accepted lead 0a45ddb2 (116.793080), whose own lineage is cbadde77 -> 6ecec8e3 -> cf6d45a8 -> 0a45ddb2; all four are declared as dependencies. Every identity, size, itemisation, bound, cap, price and toy result is restated and re-verified in THIS package; nothing is inherited by citation. This revision (v12) answers the v11 review's two objections: (1) v11's 'provable cross-base-pair independence' claim is RETRACTED: unique factorisation removes only the STRUCTURED collisions (distinct semiprime rationals never collide as rationals), while the ACCIDENTAL mod-r collisions - at the binom(B,2)*(6L^2)^2/m scale the review correctly computes - are the uniform-draw assumption (H1) itself, and the coverage law prices them: 1 - e^{-K} counts unique hits among the 6N^2 draws at the n^2/2m birthday rate, which is the substance of the law, not a correction to it; the base-count extrapolation (two toy bases against production's 2^64) is supported EMPIRICALLY (the nb strata at 2, 4, 8 base primes show the post-correction residual does not grow with the base count), not proven; (2) the C2 depth counter is PACKED in the 5-byte head word - a 34-bit pool index and a 6-bit depth counter in 40 bits - so no separate counter array is allocated and the memory model is unchanged (2^122.806, ceiling 2^122.81; a separate 2^33-counter array would have pushed it to 2^122.83); the slot cap moves from 64 to 63 (a 64th record in a slot fails the run; the Poisson tail at 64 over all 2^117 slots is 10^-80.4), the C1 increment bound is the cap 63, and the listing pays the packing honestly: the baby insert extracts and rebuilds the head word (owner-side 20 instructions), the giant lookup extracts the index (owner-side 12), giving the listing 131/123 charged at 150 - a 14.5 percent margin, the same discipline as before (v11 charged 148 over 129/122). Standing from v10/v11 unchanged: the complete preprocessing composition at its computed ceiling 2^115.7446, the census fit with BOTH parameters reported (|dev| ~ 0.235/L + 0.000514, the L->infinity floor 5.14e-4 stated, the 0.0015 allowance at 2.9x that floor), and the scalar multiplication at 662 with the window table's affine normalisation at the standard batch-inversion cost.
work_function: W(n) for n >= 2^20 equals W(2^20) = records + per-node fixed work + comparisons + gap tables + candidate re-walk (including both table rebuilds) + strand starts + segment starts + status tree + base H-primes + walk list + split gaps + candidate multiplications + kept blocks + candidate copy + Lemma 1, with records = 2N x 2000 x (1 + 150/2000), N = 64424840203624563870472181515288576 = 2^64 x L per side (L = 3492477585540061 steps, all w distinct), m = (r-1)/2^20, K = 4980/10000; the attack reads only A_1 and A_d. W(2^20) = 138952126879005574743392831454772147 units exactly. Score = ceil(10^6 log2 W)/10^6 = 116.742072 = 116742072/1000000.
heuristics: H1 (coverage; the load-bearing heuristic): the 6N^2(1 - (L-1)/L^2) independent rationals a w/(u a' w') hit z = s^d like uniform elements of the order-m subgroup H, so the success probability is at least 1 - e^{-K} = 0.39226 at the lower bound K = 0.498 (the realised 6N^2/m is 0.498 x (1 + 2^-54), N = 64424840203624563870472181515288576 = 2^64 x L exactly). Support: Lemma 4 (the six-fold symmetry and the parity key make the six orbit images of one record share one key and one comparison), the L-entry walk list giving exactly N = 2^64 x L distinct scalars per side, the diagonal collapse K' = K(1 - (L-1)/L^2), the three coverage toys (z = +0.43/+0.94/-1.43), and the load-bearing L- and base-stratified exact-coverage census: twenty-six genuine primes with 6d | r-1 (twenty at two base primes in four growing L strata, six more at four and eight base primes), the exact covered set C = {b*u/g mod r_t} enumerated on each, the post-correction residual shrinking monotonically with L and fitting the two-parameter model 0.235/L + 0.000514 with the L->infinity floor 5.14e-4 reported (rms scatter 0.00136), no systematic bias (signed means +0.0013 or below in every stratum; 16 positive, 10 negative overall), the wrap flag reported per row with the wrapping and non-wrapping subsets in agreement (mean |dev| 0.0023 vs 0.0024), and the residual not growing with the base-prime count (0.00237 at nb = 2, 0.00137 at nb = 4, 0.00077 at nb = 8) - with the cross-block statement made honestly: unique factorisation removes only the structured collisions, while the accidental collisions are the uniform-draw assumption (H1) itself, priced by the law.

H2 and H2' (supply): a fraction 1/2^20 of primes near q are H-primes (q^m = 1 mod r); gaps between consecutive H-primes are exponential with mean 2^20 ln q, so the L-th (L = 2^51.6332) H-prime above 2^39 is below 2^78 and a gap above 2^33 among the listed ones has probability < 2^-167 per list (such gaps split into two table entries against the reserve). The base-prime search interval [2^80, F] is sized by the fixed point X = 2^66*2^20*ln(F) (X ~ 2^92.0), so the integrand bound 1/ln(q) >= 1/ln(F) gives an expected supply of at least 2^66 against the 2^65 requirement, the shortfall the Chernoff tail C9 under H2'' (independent membership indicators). Checked by the run's H-prime sanity block: 402 of the 6542 primes below 2^16 are sixteenth powers against 408.875 expected (binomial z = -0.34).

H3 (key bits): the 192-bit parity-selected y keys of the walked points behave like independent uniform strings across the six-element mu_6 orbits. This is a heuristic about coordinates of structured points; the end-to-end toy bins 16-bit truncated keys into 32 pseudo-nodes x 16 heads and reports occupancy chi^2 = 24.27 on 31 degrees of freedom (z = -0.85).

Caps C1-C9 (ours, every tail rounded towards the larger probability): C1 comparisons per node - Bernstein for bounded increments, each giant lookup contributing one head-slot occupancy in [0, 63] (the C2 cap; the 6-bit depth counter is packed in the 40-bit head word) with variance bound 63 mu, evaluated at the C3-envelope worst mean mu x (1 + 2^-9) against the 1.01 x mu cap: per-node tail 2^-953.1, over all 2^84 nodes 2^-869.1; C2 head-slot depth (cap 63 - a 64th record fails the run; Poisson 0.388, tail 10^-80.4 over 2^117 slots; the counter lives in the packed head word, no separate array); C3 node record-count deviations (Chernoff 2^-2971 over all nodes; the deviation's cost is carried inside C1, which is evaluated at the envelope's worst mean); C4 false candidate pairs - a compared pair already agrees on the 84 routing and 33 slot key bits, so false matches cost 2^-75 per comparison, expected N^2/2^192 = 2^39.27, cap 2^44 with Chernoff tail (e mu/t)^t = 2^-5.7e13; C5 true matches, two channels - off-diagonal Poisson(0.498) tail exp(-1.42e7) = 2^-2.0e7 at the 2^20 cap, and the diagonal challenges z = a/a' which abort at the caps with union probability 6*2^128/m = 2^-104.27 (the same single event that would break C4 and C7); C6 candidate sinks (owner candidate lists, tail 2^-3.9e6; generating-node kept-block receive, tail 2^-3.8e7); C7 re-walk key repeats (the retained key already occurs, so >= 5 kept steps need 4 further hits: L^5/(5! 2^768) per chain, 2^-451.7 over all chains); C8 node overflow (capacity 2^33.32 baby records against mean 2^31.63 per node; 2^-20 budgeted for modelling); C9 base-prime supply (Chernoff 2^-1.3e19 at delta = 1/2 under H2''). Together charged 2^-40.

Success arithmetic: 1 - e^{-K} = 0.39226 at the lower-bound K = 0.498, minus the 2^-40 cap union, minus the 2^-20 C8 modelling budget, minus a 0.0015 census-informed allowance (the census's post-correction residual fits 0.235/L over L = 74 to 295; 0.0015 is the fitted residual at L = 159, so the two-parameter fit |dev| ~ 0.235/L + 0.000514 gives an L->infinity floor of 5.14e-4 and the allowance is 2.9x that floor, with the per-prime scatter (rms 0.00136) a toy-scale mod-r coincidence effect whose expected count does not grow with the modulus) = 0.39075, claimed at 0.3907 against the 0.39 required.
limitations: This is an analytic bound, not a full-size execution.

H1 and H3 are validated at toy scale only (the three coverage toys, the L-stratified exact-coverage census and the end-to-end run in this package's own evidence). The census's production extrapolation is a measured 1/L fit over a fourfold L range, not a proof; the 0.0015 allowance prices the fit as if production L were 159.

Instruction counts are itemised analytic counts from an AArch64-scalar-style listing at six 64-bit limbs per field element, not hardware measurements; every shared price (the F_r-multiplication at 383, the inversion at 2^16 by the full binary extended Euclid (four six-limb values, coefficient maintenance included), the projective 4-bit-window scalar multiplication at 662 including the window table's affine normalisation at the standard batch-inversion cost (3(n-1) + 4n multiplications plus one inversion), the Tonelli-Shanks square root at 2048, the modexp at 512) is derived as a worst-case bound in proof.md section 3 with its algorithm, and the cluster model is the accepted lineage's definition restated. The unit convention is the organiser's own normalisation clause: COST_MODEL.md's prices are 'rounded organizer normalization constants ... not CPU timings or exact measured instruction counts' and candidate_prices_allowed is false, so non-group work is charged as itemised instructions over the pinned 2000-instruction reference budget.

Memory is exponential, as for any BSGS-form Cheon attack: the exact integer sum is 2^122.806 bytes (the retained 2^32 x 96-byte gap table per generating node and the 40-byte linked pool records included), claimed at its ceiling 2^122.81.

The per-record charge 150 is an itemised analytic count over a 33-line six-limb listing whose maximal variant is 131/123 (a 14.5 percent margin, the same discipline as the lead's 26 percent over its listed 143, where the lead charged 180); it is not a hardware measurement. The score sits 0.0510 bits under the accepted lead and 0.0192 under the pending fork entry 116.761224; the gain is the lead's own published slack (K = 0.498 against the lead's 0.52, charge 150 against the lead's 180 at comparable 14.5/26 percent margins) net of the honest repricing this package adds (the scalar-mul 640 -> 662 window-table normalisation at the standard batch cost, and the packed-head-word listing cost); a reviewer who prices any line differently gets a different number and the ledger is a single script.
